items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I did quite a few gigs with Kaiser and Bossman.

ctx.x: Soon after that, Timmie, was in no condition to go anywhere else to try and get us a job because his face broke out with some kind of infection and as I was not the go-getter type, the band never got it's foot off the ground and that was my only venture in the band leading business in the States. I suppose that I was just not born to be a leader in those days.

Then I started hanging around the Rhythmn Club again and managed to pick a few gigs with Kaiser Marshall, the first well known drummer of the Fletcher Henderson orchestra. And there was a little fellow who played alto sax not very well who was named Leon Gross, but all the musicians called him Bossman, who got quite a few gigs also. Times were difficult as the Depression was still on in the USA, and musicians accepted jobs for whatever price they could get.

Kaiser called a dollar a potato and when he would ask me if I would do a gig with him, he would explain that the job only paid three potatoes. And there was a saying amongst musicians that if you did not want the gig, there was a boy around the corner that would accept it. And I was one of the boys around the corner....I did quite a few
